newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks down 3.76 pct to new 98-mth low.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks down 3.76 pct to new 98-mth low.

text.p: Thai stocks ended sharply lower at a new 98-month low on Thursday on concern about the future of the government's economic policies folloiwng the resignation of Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan, brokers said.
"The resignation of Amnuay worsened the already-bearish sentiment," Somchai Trairattanapirom, vice president at SITCA Investment and Securities.
The composite SET index finished 18.17 points at 464.77 on 5.9 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index was down 1.70 points to 31.90.
"Investors are now worrying about the continuation of government's economic policies as well as its stability," Somchai said.
Amnuay on Thursday resigned from his finance minister post after rifts between him and political rivals from within the government's six-party over his handling of the ailing economy.
His ally and commerce minister Narongchai Akrasanee also tendered his resignation effective June 21.
Decliners led advancers 262 to 69 with 64 remained unchanged.
Brokers said the market sentiment will remain weak tomorrow as most investors will await the announcement of new finance minister.
Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Thursday that he would name a new finance minister to replace the outgoing Amnuay Viravan on Friday (June 20) to oversee the troubled national economy.

He also told a news conference that there would be no change in the current policy of defending the baht against speculative attacks and that finance and foreign exchange stability were his government's top priority.
Bangkok Bank dropped nine baht to 102 on the top active trade of 734 million baht.
Thai Farmers Bank shed 5.50 to 73 and Siam Commercial Bank fell seven to 79.
Advanced Info Service slid 13 to 134. Blue-chip Siam Cement was down 32 to 366.
